rules.sentence: Children who fail to improve—marked by persistent pain, fever, or inability to tolerate a diet—should undergo prompt surgical intervention.
The nonoperative protocol generally includes 1 to 2 days of intravenous broad-spectrum antibiotics, followed by a 7- to 10-day course of oral antibiotics if clinical improvement occurs.
Appendicitis is classified as complicated when there is gross perforation, presence of a fecalith, abscess, or frank purulence in the abdomen.[38]
